elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Rendered Article XXII now reads "NO RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL The Licensor shall have no right of first refusal or right to match." The notice obligation, the five-business-day Exercise Period and Licensor's ability to take the third-party offer are all deleted, so no most-favoured-offer or matching mechanic burdening Licensee (Customer) survives. The remaining sentence confers a right on Licensee, not an obligation to Licensor.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no Customer-side MFN/match obligation at all ("The Licensor shall have no right of first refusal or right to match"), so there is no scope left to confine to a defined product. Nothing elsewhere in the cited text imposes a pricing MFN on Licensee (Articles V-VIII are the tiered fee table; the Revisions clause runs in Customer's favour).

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the "During the term of this Agreement" duration hook was removed together with the grant, and no residual Customer MFN/match obligation remains to be time-limited.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with the obligation deleted outright there is no comparison exercise for Licensee to perform, so no like-for-like carve-out is required.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative grant of the Right of First Refusal / right to match against third-party asset-sale or merger offers, the Licensee notice trigger and the Exercise Period are all struck, which is exactly the playbook remedy ("Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN"). No Vendor-granted MFN existed to preserve.
Fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because the obligation they would constrain no longer exists; they impose no further drafting work.

Minimality holds. The edit is confined to Article XXII, the article that contains the offending mechanic. The Customer-favourable second sentence (Licensee's right to consummate the third-party transaction) is retained rather than deleted, and its restatement is necessary rather than cosmetic: the original sentence hung on the now-deleted defined terms "Right of First Refusal" and "Exercise Period", so repair was required to avoid a dangling antecedent. No survival tail, expense language, damages category or unrelated boilerplate was added.

Intent is preserved. The "Subject to the Change Of Control and Assignment Sections" qualifier prevents the restated sentence from reading as an unconditional freedom to sell that would contradict the retained consent provisions at p0134 and p0149; it narrows rather than expands Customer's rights and creates no new Vendor right. Nothing in the removed text allocated fees, timing or remedies elsewhere.

Two drafting points to tighten (not defects that change the outcome): (i) the instrument uses Article numbering ("ARTICLE XXII"), so conform the cross-reference to "Articles" (ideally with the article numbers for Change of Control and Assignment) rather than "Sections", to avoid an imprecise reference; and (ii) confirm by a document-wide search that the defined terms "Right of First Refusal" and "Exercise Period", which existed only in Article XXII, are not used anywhere else - if they are, those references must be conformed or they will dangle.
